what.text: This page follows asylum seekers from the Democratic Republic of the Congo in South Africa: people who have asked for international protection and are waiting for a decision.
At the end of 2025, UNHCR counted 22207 of these asylum seekers in South Africa, 13.2% of all asylum seekers from the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
Refugees from the country, a separate group, live mostly in Uganda, Burundi, Zambia and Rwanda.

why.text: UCDP records armed conflict over the government of DR Congo in periods from 1996, at war level in many years, and in every year from 2016 to 2025.
From 2016 to 2025 the opponents it records include Kamuina Nsapu, RNL, CNPSC and M23, and it also records armed conflict with the Islamic State group from 2017 to 2025.

when.text: UNHCR's series for this group starts in 2000 at 759 asylum seekers.
The figure was at its highest, 36120, at the end of 2019, and the main years of displacement in the data are 2005 and 2017 to 2025.

how.text: The sources don't say which routes people took or where they live in South Africa.
Asylum seekers are counted separately from refugees, as year-end totals for South Africa only.
